messages.subject: dplyr wish list
parts:
I suppose this is mostly for Hadley, Romain, etc, but I wanted to post it here to get any further comments, and I don't think these are
specific enough for pull requests:

1) I've never been sure why you'd use select instead of transmute.  I think it would be simpler to just rename transmute into select.

2) I think this may have been requested before, but it would be _very_ handy to have something like

mutate_filter( filter expression, mutate expression) that mutates records that satisfy a filter condition.

It would be equivalent (in loose sql) to update tbl set <mutate expressions> where <filter expression>.
I realize you need to set any new columns to NA for rows which do not satisfy the filter and that you can do the same thing with
the idiom
rbind(filter(dt,!condition),filter(dt,condition) %>% mutate), but that's pretty ugly for such a simple thing, and it doens't
preserve previous "arrange" operations.

2a)  I've gotten around this in the past using rowwise %>% mutate(value=ifelse(condition,newvalue,value)) but I don't know how
to "unrowwise" without going back to a dataframe.  That idiom still is uglier than the suggestion above.

3) Along those lines, it would be nice to be able to update dataframes in joins, e.g.

left_join(dta,dtb,update=T) which take dtb's values iff they match in dta. 

Again, could be done with rbinds, or using data.table's' syntax rbindlist(list(a[!b],b),use.names=TRUE,fill=FALSE), but I think
amending left_join would be a lot cleaner.

If I'm missing a nifty way to do these operations, please let me know!

messages.subject: Re: dplyr wish list
parts: On Friday, June 5, 2015 at 2:18:55 PM UTC-5, Seth Wayland wrote:
For 3) I think D Holmes is asking for an update join. Something like this: http://stackoverflow.com/q/1293330

Seth

3) Yes that's what I'm looking for.  All I want to do is update a tbl with potentially duplicate data. I figured out a (less than elegant) way of doing what I'm looking for:
 
> a1=data_frame(a=c("A","B","C"),b=1:3)
> a2=data_frame(a=c("B","C"),b=c(4,3))
> rbind(a2,anti_join(a1,a2,by=c("a"))) %>% arrange(a)
Source: local data frame [3 x 2]

  a b
1 A 1
2 B 4
3 C 3

  Ideally, there would be an option on left_join which would return (to use an sqlism) var=coalesce(var.x, var.y) for all common variables which are not keys.

2)  The referenced thread is exactly what I'm looking for.  It could be considered a variant of the above.

1) The way I see it,

select(newname1=oldname1,oldname2, oldname3) is a subset of  transmute(newname1=f(oldname1),oldname2,oldname3)

I realize transmute is really mutate %>% select, but renaming transmute as select would simplify a lot of code.
